evidence: Cic. Off. 2.51: nocentem aliquando, modo nē nefārium impiumque dēfendere
terms.comment: The opposite of innocēns; as a noun, a guilty person.

terms.gloss: guilty; as a noun, the guilty, offenders
terms.comment: As an adjective mostly in the poets; in prose chiefly the noun (Lewis & Short).
To be found guilty, condemnārī or damnārī.

phrases.latin: innocēns, sī accūsātus sit, absolvī potest, nocēns, nisi accūsātus fuerit, condemnārī nōn potest
phrases.english: an innocent man, if he is accused, can be acquitted; a guilty one cannot be found guilty unless he has been accused
Was he acquitted or found guilty?

sources: Lewis & Short: noceo · Lewis & Short: sons · Lewis & Short: condemno
